sources.title: Radio Waves
sources.locator: What are radio waves?; receiver and speaker mechanical vibrations
sources.summary: Radio is electromagnetic. A receiver converts a radio signal into mechanical vibrations through speakers.

sources.title: Water Density
sources.locator: Ice is less dense than water
sources.summary: Ordinary ice has an open lattice, is less dense than liquid water, and floats. Density is mass per volume.
sources.material_reuse: Facts paraphrased; no site images used

sources.title: FAQs About Water and Steam
sources.locator: What is the structure of a water molecule?; Why does liquid water have a density maximum?
sources.summary: Hydrogen bonding stabilizes an open ice network. Freezing increases volume, producing lower density than liquid water.

sources.title: Why Is the Sky Blue?
sources.locator: Main explanation; What makes a red sunset?
sources.summary: Sunlight contains visible colors. Air scatters shorter blue wavelengths more than red. At sunset a longer atmospheric path removes more blue from the direct beam.
sources.caveat: Intro compares blue with all colors; use narrower blue-versus-red comparison to avoid violet error

sources.title: Why Is The Sky Blue?
sources.locator: Explanation before So why are sunrises and sunsets red?; sunset section
sources.summary: Rayleigh scattering redirects blue/violet more than red. White sunlight contains a range of wavelengths; a longer direct path at sunset changes its color.

sources.title: Anatomy of an Electromagnetic Wave
sources.locator: What are Electromagnetic and Mechanical waves?; ELECTROMAGNETIC WAVES
sources.summary: Mechanical disturbances propagate through material; sound cannot cross an ideal vacuum. Radio is electromagnetic and can propagate in vacuum.

sources.title: Cosmicopia: Energy Traveling Through Space
sources.locator: 12. Sound in Space; 13. Tuning Fork in Space; Radio waves
sources.summary: Sound is a pressure wave; spacecraft air permits speech. A vibrating object in vacuum does not send airborne sound to another person. Radio carries communications.

sources.title: LISTEN UP!
sources.locator: Paragraphs beginning But how can there be sounds; However, there are radio waves
sources.summary: Sound needs material; electromagnetic radio needs no material and equipment converts received radio to speaker sound.

sources.title: How loud is space?
sources.locator: Opening sentence and Acoustic Diagnostics explanation
sources.summary: Vacuum cannot transmit sound while the inside of a spacecraft can be noisy.
